subject: maths
question: A alone can complete a work in 20 days with full efficiency. If the efficiency of A decreases by 20 percent, then A alone can do the same work in how many days?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Efficiency** ratio (Initial : New) = 100% : 80% = 5 : 4

**Time** is inversely proportional to efficiency: Time ratio = 4 : 5

Given: 4 units of time = 20 days

1 unit = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 days

New time = 5 units = 5 × 5 = 25 days

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial time = 20 days, **Efficiency** decrease = 20%.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cce4a7dc9aaa39a9e0361a96392676bbe64a939e16e8d1771141dcc4d3f7b3b.png] 

⇒ Let the initial **efficiency** of A be 100 units/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = Efficiency × Time = 100 × 20 = 2000 units.

⇒ New **efficiency** of A = 100 − (20% of 100) = 80 units/day.

⇒ **New Time** taken = Total Work ÷ New Efficiency

⇒ New Time = 2000 ÷ 80 = 25 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion in Work

When **Total Work** is constant, the time required to complete the work is inversely proportional to the **efficiency** (T ∝ 1/E).

Percentage and Time

If efficiency increases by x%, the new time is T ÷ (1 + x/100). If efficiency decreases by x%, the new time is T ÷ (1 − x/100).

Work Equivalence Formula

M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is efficiency/number of workers, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.</p
